kind.rationale: PR #586 already is a backend module with one XRPL icUSD lane; no XRPL bridge instance and no second XRPL token (design section 1.4).

standard.rationale: PR #586 implements an escrow-backed trust-line issued currency with exact decimal parsing and caps. D2 (settled for planning) keeps that lane; Multi-Purpose Token is deferred, not a replacement gate.

value.basis: 15 significant digits (D7 planning decision): both each operation and total outstanding stay at or below 999999999999999 e8s, and inexact amounts are rejected or held exactly, never rounded.

signed_payload.value: Ed25519 over the 0x53545800 prefix followed by the canonical serialization without TxnSignature; no pre-hash.

value.text: The issuer account must be funded from outside: 1 XRP base reserve plus 0.2 XRP per owned object.
Holders must create a trust line to the issuer before they can receive icUSD.

open_decisions.topic: XRPL trust-line token (PR #586) or Multi-Purpose Token

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): XRPL uses PR #586's issued-currency escrow and import seam; MPT is deferred, not a replacement gate; the no-vault canonical return stays a named missing implementation.
Design section 12 (settled for planning): conservative 15-significant-digit caps (999999999999999 e8s) on each operation AND on total outstanding, with exact rejection or holding of inexact amounts.

open_decisions.topic: Testnet escrow: real icUSD ledger or a test ledger

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): synthetic test ledgers for future testnet demos; no real canonical icUSD is locked for a new testnet rollout under this groundwork.

activation_blockers.text: PR #586 is open and unmerged and its issuance lane is disabled by default. Nothing here claims deployment.

No dedicated no-vault operation returns XRPL icUSD to an ICP account in the PR #586 endpoint list. It is specified as a follow-up (BB-37), not an edit to #586. The return source (BB-56, with the BB-57 cases) is accepted at source and focused-test level on a separate local branch that was not pushed (local commits up to 46cf6b34). It is not in PR #586, not on this branch and not in PR #591. Still held: publication of that branch (the exact push was denied and is not retried here), the PR #586 merge, deployment, and live or public-chain evidence.
activation_blockers.source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-multichain-icusd-groundwork-design.md section 1.4; BB-56 e48dc18d and BB-57 46cf6b34 (unpublished local branch, not pushed)

activation_blockers.text: The PR #586 frontend supports Xaman only (manual address or QR fallback). No other XRPL wallet connector was found.

Missing on PR #586 and on this branch. A local follow-up accepted at source and focused-test level (BB-55, f887fab5 with 868ebca8) wires the validator on a separate local branch that was not pushed; it is not in PR #586, this branch or PR #591. On the PR #586 baseline (before that follow-up), the 15-digit request validator (validate_normal_request and parse_normal_request) has no caller outside tests, and the frontend parser accepts up to u64. On that baseline, the 15-digit bound holds only if a controller sets both caps at or below 999999999999999 e8s.

Missing on PR #586 and on this branch. The BB-55 follow-up (f887fab5 with 868ebca8), on a separate local branch that was not pushed, clamps the caps and checks the ceiling before any new attempt; it is not in PR #586, this branch or PR #591. On the PR #586 baseline (before that follow-up), config accepts any u64 for both caps, and the requirement was to clamp both to 999999999999999 e8s when applying config and again inside the per-operation check and the return-intent creation, add the issuer snapshot ceiling as a coverage condition, and clamp in the frontend parser before an amount is shown. The holder trust-line limit defaults to the outstanding cap, so an unclamped cap writes a limit longer than 15 digits.

Missing on PR #586 and on this branch. The BB-55 follow-up (f887fab5), on a separate local branch that was not pushed, counts pending imports; it is not in PR #586, this branch or PR #591. On the PR #586 baseline (before that follow-up), an import still in its ledger-pull phase is neither in the delivery bucket nor a reservation, so concurrent imports can each pass the cap check and together exceed the total cap (from reading the source, not tested). The requirement was to count pending-pull amounts and re-check when the import advances.

Implementation missing. The outstanding counter has no origin split between imported and debt-originated units after delivery. Report cumulative delivered by kind and never claim a per-token origin or a debt-free outstanding; only the import flow carries no new debt.

The issuer policy (allow clawback, no freeze) has no default and cannot change once setup starts. Both options are irreversible, so choosing one is a decision before setup, and the page must disclose the choice. Local fixtures use false and false, which is not a production decision.

The backend code section was 9,648,104 bytes (77% of the 12 MiB limit) after merging main, and PocketIC 7 caps the code section at 10 MiB, leaving about 837,656 bytes for the follow-up. Budget the follow-up against the smaller figure.
The controller and upgrade-authority model for this instance and its chain-side authorities is not decided (D6). The controller set is the root of trust for escrow and every signature.

One of the three mainnet read hosts uses port 51234, and support for non-443 ports in HTTPS outcalls is not established. PR #586 treats that host as possibly unreachable and requires a spare 443 provider, so quorum 2 stays reachable on the other two.

value.typical_wait: validated ledger with tesSUCCESS; wait time not stated in the facts files

min_quorum.rationale: PR #586 reads need READ_QUORUM = 2 identical reduced responses.

outcall_notes.value: Reads and submits go through HTTPS outcalls to rippled JSON-RPC with a read quorum of 2 identical reduced responses. No official ICP canister exists for XRPL, and non-443 port support is not established.
